title: POC scoping: scope, benchmarks, credits & contracting
summary: AE + SE scoped a 2-week pilot for BrightPath Health to validate latency and cost targets on their triage assistant workload. Agreed success metrics (p99 latency < 250ms for short prompts, throughput 200 concurrent users, quality gates by automated evals). Redwood to provide 2M token pilot credits, a benchmark plan, and a contracting checklist. Next steps: pricing sheet, security pack, run bench tests next week, follow up procurement timeline.
next_steps: Redwood to send pilot pricing spreadsheet + 2M credits breakdown (Samir) - due 2025-06-20
SE to share benchmark harness and seed prompt set (Ethan) - due 2025-06-19
Customer to provide sample production prompts and traffic profile (Monica) - due 2025-06-20
Schedule 90-min benchmark run (Zoom + perf dashboard) - target 2025-06-24

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: 57 mins | Attendees: Samir, Ethan (Redwood); Monica, Daniel, Priya (BrightPath)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Samir from Redwood, with Ethan, our SE. Monica?
[00:06] Monica: Yep, Monica here, hi. Daniel and Priya on our side as well.
[00:10] Samir: Great. Goal today is to align on POC scope, success criteria, and the commercial pilot terms — credits, length, and how we transition to contracting.
[00:20] Monica: Sounds good. We're really focused on the triage assistant — short form prompts, a fair amount of structured output, and we need this to be fast for clinicians.
[00:30] Ethan: Cool, can you give ballpark traffic? concurrency, tokens per request, that kind of thing?
[00:34] Daniel: Sure. Peak conc around 150-200 concurrent users, average request is ~250 tokens in, 100 tokens out, but we have bursts where it goes to 600 tokens in.
[00:44] Monica: Latency sensitivity is high — user expectations are sub-second for the UI. We can tolerate a little more if quality is better but want to quantify it.
[00:55] Ethan: Helpful. For POC we typically run a focused benchmark that mirrors your 95/99th percentile flows. Suggested success metrics: p95/p99 latency targets, throughput (reqs/sec), and a quality gate measured by evals on a seed prompt set.
[01:08] Priya: From security — we need SOC2 details, audit log retention, KMS integration, and clarity on data residency. We'll need that before any production contract.
[01:18] Samir: Absolutely. We'll include the security pack link in the follow-up (notes: security-pack.pdf). KMS is supported, and for the pilot we can do encrypted at rest with customer-provided KMS in Private deployments; hosted also has enterprise KMS options.
[01:33] Monica: For the POC, we prefer hosted but isolated; we need assurance logs are accessible.
[01:38] Ethan: We can provide token-level cost and latency breakdown in the console and export logs. For the tests, we'll enable KV cache to mimic production prompt sequences — helps cut downstream token usage by heavy reuse.
[01:52] Daniel: Quick question: does Redwood's runtime handle continuous batching? In our sim the requests are short and bursty.
[01:58] Ethan: Yes, continuous batching and dynamic batching by model. We also have autoscale on Dedicated pools; for a pilot we typically run on a dedicated small pool to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
[02:10] Monica: What's the recommended pilot length? We were thinking 2 weeks.
[02:15] Samir: Two weeks is standard. We'll propose a 2-week pilot with 2 million token credits. That should cover realistic bench runs and some early user testing. If you anticipate more, we can adjust.
[02:26] Monica: 2M tokens — can you break down what that translates to in cost if we go to production?
[02:31] Samir: Yes, we'll send a pilot pricing sheet and a projected production estimate scaled to your daily volume. For the pilot credits we won't bill for overage within pre-agreed limits; anything beyond we'll flag first.
[02:41] Daniel: For success criteria, we want: p99 latency < 250ms for under-300-token prompts, throughput to support 200 concurrent users with <5% error rate, and a quality pass rate of >90% on our automated eval set. Is that reasonable?
[02:57] Ethan: Those are reasonable targets for smaller open models on high-end GPUs; for larger context or longer outputs p99 will naturally increase. We should scope specific prompt buckets: short triage, long case summaries, and multi-turn follow-ups.
[03:12] Monica: Okay, let's lock those buckets. We'll provide sample prompts.
[03:18] Ethan: Great. I'll prepare a benchmark plan: test harness, seed prompts, how to run load tests, and a dashboard to visualize p50/p95/p99, token usage, and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:32] Priya: Also please document retention windows and how to redact PHI in the logs for the sample exports.
[03:39] Samir: Noted. We'll remit a redacted export guide.
[03:44] Daniel: On contracting — we have procurement timelines. Typical procurement is 6-8 weeks after pilot sign-off, but if we can get an SOW and estimate early, it shortens.
[03:55] Samir: Understood. Our standard path: pilot -> SOW + pilot results -> estimates & legal redlines -> PO. We can provide an accelerated SOW template and a contracting checklist.
[04:06] Monica: On commercial guardrails, we need clear pilot terms: credit amount, duration, what happens on overages, and what the success exit criteria are to convert to a paid pilot or contract.
[04:18] Samir: We'll send a pilot T&C doc. Proposed guardrails: 14-day pilot, 2M token credits, a single test run per day for bench ramping, overage alerting and approval flow before extra billing, and a conversion path tied to agreed success metrics.
[04:32] Monica: Works. A question about fallback: if latency breaches targets in pilot, do we have options? switch models, enable quantization, or move to Dedicated?
[04:40] Ethan: All of the above. We'll try model variants (smaller / quantized) first, enable more aggressive caching, and if needed run on Dedicated GPU pool or add burst capacity. We'll document the tradeoffs in throughput vs quality.
[04:57] Daniel: Bench plan detail — what metrics do you gather automatically vs need us to instrument?
[05:02] Ethan: Automatics: per-request latency, tokens in/out, model variant, host/region, error codes. We'll ask you to tag requests with a workload id so we can split short vs long prompts. For quality we run closed evals and WER/semantic similarity metrics and your own rubric.
[05:18] Monica: We'll create a 300-sample seed set and a 200-sample edge-case set. Hope that's enough.
[05:24] Ethan: Good starting point. For throughput simulation we'll replay anonymized logs if you can export them.
[05:31] Monica: We'll work on that.
[05:34] Samir: Commercial ask — do you have an internal threshold for pilot spend to approve pilots without a PO?
[05:40] Daniel: Under $10k usually green-lit; above that we need procurement sign-off. How does 2M credits map financially?
[05:47] Samir: Depends on model selection; as a rough estimate, 2M tokens on a mid-range open model equates to ~$3-5k list equivalent; on larger models maybe $10-12k. We'll give a model-specific estimate in the sheet.
[05:59] Priya: For compliance we need to see the SOC2 report and encryption spec before we run anything with production data. Is that in the security pack?
[06:06] Samir: Yes, SOC2 + ISO90? ISO27001 — sorry, ISO27001 — both included in the pack. Also KMS integration doc and minimum retention controls. We'll attach links.
[06:18] Monica: Fine. For the pilot data, we can anonymize the sample logs.
[06:22] Ethan: Perfect. Plan for next week: Ethan will kick off the benchmark harness and share instructions; Samir will send the pricing and pilot T&Cs; Monica to share sample prompts and anonymized logs by Friday. We'll then run a 48-hour warmup and a 24-48 hour soak + targeted p99 runs.
[06:38] Daniel: Timeline sounds good. Procurement sync planned for week after pilot end.
[06:44] Samir: If pilot meets success metrics we can draft SOW and provide a committed reserved capacity pricing option for Dedicated or a volume-based hosted discount.
[06:53] Monica: On measurement for quality, we'll have the automated eval, plus a small human review sample for edge cases.
[06:59] Ethan: Recommended: 95% automated pass + manual review under 5% failure for edgecases.
[07:06] Priya: Anything about data residency? We need EU data to land in Frankfurt region for PHI, is that supported?
[07:12] Ethan: We support regional routing in hosted and Private for on-prem. For EU region we can pin instances to eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 equivalents; detail in the deployment docs.
[07:22] Monica: Great. Any competitors you compared this against in pilot pricing?
[07:27] Samir: Customers often benchmark Anthropic and OpenAI for quality vs cost, and AWS SageMaker for self-hosted controls. We'll include competitor notes.
[07:36] Daniel: Ok. Mechanically, how do we kick off the bench run? Who runs it?
[07:40] Ethan: We provide the harness and runbooks. We typically run the load from Redwood infra to remove local network variables, but we can also run from your infra if you prefer. For latency-sensitive tests, run from your region to get realistic numbers.
[07:53] Monica: We'll probably want Redwood to run the heavy tests and we will run a small set locally to sanity-check.
[07:59] Samir: Fine. I'll schedule a 90-min run/walkthrough on 2025-06-24 to watch the first bench results live.
[08:07] Monica: Works. One final ask — can we get a binding commitment on the pilot credits not being used for any other customer?
[08:13] Samir: Pilot credits are allocated to your account and not shared; we'll put the allocation in writing in the T&C.
[08:21] Daniel: What about SLA during pilot?
[08:24] Ethan: For pilots we don't expose enterprise SLA, but we commit to reasonable availability for the test and active engineering support. For production we can discuss SLA tiers in the SOW.
[08:36] Priya: Ok, we'll review the security pack and get back with any gaps.
[08:40] Samir: Perfect. To recap: 14-day pilot, 2M token credits, benchmark plan, security pack, and a procurement checklist. Follow-ups due next week.
[08:51] Monica: Thanks everyone.
[08:53] Daniel: Thanks.
[08:55] Samir: Thanks, end call.

Notes & links shared during call: pricing-sheet.xlsx (will be attached), security-pack.pdf, benchmark-harness-instructions.md, sample-prompt-set.csv (seed).
